title: Evaluating a source (ROBOT)
intent: formative · pattern spot-the-error / source-evaluation · a media-literacy lens
statement: The same source through a misinformation lens. Work ROBOT — Reliability, Objective, Bias, Ownership, Type — one check at a time, and stamp a verdict on each.

source.title: “Why Solar Will Power Everything by 2027”
source.meta: greenfuturenow.blog · no author listed · posted 2019 · no citations

items.label: Reliability
items.question: evidence you can check?
items.verdict: Sweeping claims, no citations — nothing here is verifiable.

items.label: Objective
items.question: what is it trying to do?
items.verdict: To convince you solar wins by 2027 — a persuasive goal, not a neutral one.

items.label: Bias
items.question: whose side is it on?
items.verdict: One-sided boosterism — no trade-offs, costs or counter-evidence.

items.label: Ownership
items.question: who publishes / funds it?
items.verdict: A self-published advocacy blog — no institution or editor stands behind it.

items.label: Type
items.question: what kind of source?
items.verdict: Opinion and advocacy dressed as analysis — not reporting or scholarship.

steps.title: Meet the source
steps.text: Before judging, see what you are dealing with. Work the five ROBOT lenses in order.

steps.title: R — Reliability
steps.text: Can the claims be checked against evidence? No citations means you are taking it on faith.

steps.title: O — Objective
steps.text: What is the piece trying to achieve? A persuasive objective colours everything it selects.

steps.title: B — Bias
steps.text: Whose interests does it serve, and what does it leave out? One-sided framing is the tell.

steps.title: O — Ownership
steps.text: Who owns, funds or publishes it? An anonymous advocacy site has no accountability.

steps.title: T — Type
steps.text: Is it news, scholarship, opinion, advertising or satire? Mistaking the type misreads its authority.

steps.title: Reach a verdict
steps.text: Weigh the five together. ROBOT is built for spotting persuasion and bias — and this source is full of both.

feedForward.text: Unreliable and non-neutral — advocacy, not analysis. Treat it as evidence of hype, not of fact, and replace it with accountable, citable sources.
